  {
    "file": "junit-platform-engine/src/main/java/org/junit/platform/engine/support/hierarchical/ConcurrentHierarchicalTestExecutorService.java",
    "line": 77,
    "category": "question",
    "severity": "medium",
    "comment": "`close()` calls `shutdownNow()` without completing the futures of entries still sitting in the work queue. Can that leave a caller that is blocked in `Future.get()` or in `waitFor(...)` waiting forever? If close is only ever called after all work has drained, it would help to say so here."
  },
  {
    "file": "junit-platform-engine/src/main/java/org/junit/platform/engine/support/hierarchical/ConcurrentHierarchicalTestExecutorService.java",
    "line": 231,
    "category": "style",
    "severity": "low",
    "comment": "The trace message hardcodes \"SAME_THREAD children\", but `executeAll` is also called with the isolated tasks (the tasks requiring the global read-write lock), so the log will be misleading for that call. Pass the description in, or drop the mode from the message."
  },
  {
    "file": "junit-platform-engine/src/main/java/org/junit/platform/engine/support/hierarchical/ConcurrentHierarchicalTestExecutorService.java",
    "line": 279,
    "category": "bug",
    "severity": "medium",
    "comment": "If the thread is interrupted while blocking for the resource lock, the interrupt flag is restored but the task is silently never executed; the caller in `executeEntry` then completes the entry's future normally in its finally block, so the task is reported as finished although it never ran. Consider completing the future exceptionally (or rethrowing) on interruption."
  },
  {
    "file": "junit-platform-engine/src/main/java/org/junit/platform/engine/support/hierarchical/ConcurrentHierarchicalTestExecutorService.java",
    "line": 263,
    "category": "design",
    "severity": "low",
    "comment": "Calling `complete(null)` unconditionally in the finally block relies on it being a silent no-op after `completeExceptionally` in the catch block. That is correct but easy to misread as overwriting the failure; completing normally at the end of the try block would make the intent explicit."
  },
  {
    "file": "junit-platform-engine/src/main/java/org/junit/platform/engine/support/hierarchical/ConcurrentHierarchicalTestExecutorService.java",
    "line": 470,
    "category": "design",
    "severity": "low",
    "comment": "`incrementAttempts()` builds a new `Entry` around the *same* future, and the compact constructor registers a `whenComplete` callback on every construction. Each re-enqueue therefore attaches another completion listener to the same future, so the completion trace is logged once per attempt. Consider registering the logging callback where the future is created instead of in the constructor."
  }
]
